facts.text: Smiths Ferry got its name when Jim Smith bought the ferry from Clinton Meyers in 1891, keeping the original name.
Clinton Meyers first built a ferry across the North Fork in 1887 to move livestock to summer pastures in the Round and Long Valleys.
Logging boom hit Smiths Ferry when the Oregon Short Line Railroad arrived in the 1880s, and Coe & Carter ran camps that floated logs for railroad ties.
At 4,544 feet above sea level, Smiths Ferry sits amid the rugged Payette National Forest, surrounded by dense coniferous forests.
Smiths Ferry experiences a continental climate, with harsh snowy winters averaging 104 inches of snow and warm, dry summers reaching nearly 80°F.
